title: Silas and the Parish
premise: Estate lawyer Sable Vane, who has quietly untangled three deaths the police ruled accidental, is handed a will for a woman declared missing and presumed dead seven years ago. The will's codicil references a diary that keeps being written after the disappearance date, pointing toward a witness everyone in the parish of Hollowmere insists is dead. As Sable follows the diary's trail through the parish's tangled inheritances, he realizes the 'accidents' he solved were all connected to one family's desperate effort to bury a living heir. In the end, Sable finds the witness alive but hidden in plain sight as the parish's aging verger, exposes the patriarch who staged her death to steal her inheritance, and must choose between preserving his own anonymity and testifying publicly—a choice that finally costs him his invisibility but saves a life.
about_author: Bram Vasquez is the pen name of a former probate clerk who spent a decade watching families fracture over paper. He writes mysteries about documents that remember what people want forgotten.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: POV Sable Vane. A courier delivers a sealed will for Edith Marsh, missing seven years, with instructions to read it only at Hollowmere parish. The emotional beat: wary curiosity—the document smells like a trap, and traps are how Sable lost everything once before.

chapters.title: Hollowmere
chapters.summary: POV Sable. He arrives in the rain-soaked parish where every face seems to know him without knowing why. The vicar welcomes him too warmly; the solicitor who summoned him has just resigned. Beat: creeping unease as small courtesies reveal coordinated control.

chapters.title: The Codicil
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Reading the will aloud to the parish trustees, Sable discovers a codicil referencing a diary 'to continue until my return.' But Edith was declared dead years ago. Beat: cold shock—the legal impossibility hooks him despite himself.

chapters.title: Diary Entries After Death
chapters.summary: POV Sable, with diary excerpts interleaved. The diary's final entries are dated three years after the disappearance, describing the parish from angles only someone hiding inside it could see. Beat: exhilaration curdling into fear—someone alive wrote these.

chapters.title: Three Accidents
chapters.summary: POV Sable. He maps the deaths he previously solved onto Hollowmere: all three victims stood to inherit or testify around the Marsh estate. Beat: grim recognition that this case is the spine of everything he's been quietly undoing.

chapters.title: The Verger Who Watches
chapters.summary: POV Sable. The elderly verger, Mr. Quill, corrects a detail about Edith only an intimate would know, then denies ever meeting her. Beat: suspicion sharpening into obsession—Quill's hands shake like someone keeping a secret.

chapters.title: The Marsh Fortune
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Digging through land records, he finds the estate's inheritance rerouted through a trust controlled by patriarch Aldous Crane, Edith's uncle-by-marriage. Beat: dawning clarity about motive—money enough to kill for, twice over.

chapters.title: A Threat Delivered Politely
chapters.summary: POV Sable. An anonymous note thanks him for his discretion and encloses a photograph of Sable's old identity—the one he buried. Beat: terror; staying invisible was never really an option.

chapters.title: What the Bells Heard
chapters.summary: POV alternating Sable and Quill (unnamed). Quill's chapter reveals fragments: a night seven years ago, a boat, a scream that wasn't a scream. Beat: guilt pressing on an old man who chose silence to survive.

chapters.title: The Fourth Accident
chapters.summary: POV Sable. The resigned solicitor is found drowned in the millpond—ruled accidental within hours. Beat: rage and urgency; the parish machinery is killing faster than Sable can investigate.

chapters.title: Crane's Hospitality
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Aldous Crane hosts him lavishly, probing with charm what Sable knows. Beneath the courtesy, a warning: witnesses in Hollowmere have short tenures. Beat: cat-and-mouse tension, both men smiling over knives.

chapters.title: The Diary's Missing Year
chapters.summary: POV Sable. A torn section covers the year Edith allegedly fled. Reconstructing it from ink and paper stock, Sable proves entries were written in the parish's own vestry supplies. Beat: triumph—the writer never left.

chapters.title: Grave Without a Body
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Edith's memorial stone sits over an empty plot; the coroner's file contains no remains, only a signed statement by the current police surgeon—who trained under Crane's patronage. Beat: righteous anger at institutional rot.

chapters.title: Quill's Confession, Interrupted
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Quill agrees to talk at midnight in the bell tower; Sable arrives to find the tower door chained and smoke rising. Beat: dread spiking—he may be too late again.

chapters.title: Ashes in the Tower
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Quill survives, barely, but burns his own testimony rather than be tortured into naming names. His last words: 'She rings the bells.' Beat: grief braided with revelation—the witness is closer than anyone imagined.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Loft
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Following rope-wear and flour dust, Sable finds Edith Marsh alive above the bakery, hidden seven years by the baker's widow, writing the diary that kept her sane. Beat: overwhelming relief shadowed by fear—finding her endangers her.

chapters.title: Why She Stayed Dead
chapters.summary: POV Edith. Her chapter: Crane forged her death after she discovered he'd murdered her father; surfacing meant death, and silence meant watching him spend her inheritance. Beat: bitter cost of survival—the price was her name, her life, her grief unattended.

chapters.title: The Trap in the Will
chapters.summary: POV Sable. He realizes the will itself was Crane's bait, designed to flush out whoever still believed Edith lived—and it worked on Sable because of his old identity, which Crane has held for years. Beat: devastating reversal; he was chosen, not hired.

chapters.title: Night of the Parish Meeting
chapters.summary: POV Sable. At the annual vestry meeting, Crane moves to have the will dismissed and Sable discredited using his stolen past. Beat: cornered desperation—Sable's last move must be made in public, in front of everyone.

chapters.title: The Bell Rings
chapters.summary: POV Sable and Edith. As Crane finishes his speech, the church bell rings once—Edith walks down the aisle, alive, holding the diary. The parish gasps; Crane's composure cracks. Beat: cathartic climax, truth arriving like sound through stone.

chapters.title: Reckoning
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Confronted with the diary, the empty grave, and Quill's surviving half-testimony, Crane confesses in fury and is arrested; the complicit surgeon turns crown's evidence. Beat: hard-won justice, unsweetened by what it cost.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: POV Sable, closing with Edith. Probate settled, Edith offers Sable partnership in restoring the estate—and a reason to stop being invisible. He signs his real name for the first time in years. Beat: quiet resolution; identity, like survival, is something you choose to claim.
